lemmas.proof_markdown: For any binary word, each zero contributes $1$ and each one contributes $-1$, so $S(c)=n-2\operatorname{wt}(c)$. Hence $\operatorname{wt}(c)\ge D$ iff $S(c)\le n-2D=2^{21}$. The two-sided bound $|S(c)|\le2^{21}$ similarly gives $D\le\operatorname{wt}(c)\le n-D$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For $n=2^{30}$, $D=2^{29}-2^{20}=535{,}822{,}336$, and $c\in\mathbb F_2^n$, let $S(c)=\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^{c_j}$. Then $\operatorname{wt}(c)\ge D$ if and only if $S(c)\le2^{21}$, and $|S(c)|\le2^{21}$ implies $D\le\operatorname{wt}(c)\le n-D$.
lemmas.title: Target signed-sum normalization

lemmas.proof_markdown: For $p_0$, repeated squaring gives $Z^{2^8}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z$ and $Z^{2^{16}}\equiv Z$. Writing $h=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3$, Euclidean division ends with remainders $Z^2+1$ and $1$, so $\gcd(p_0,Z^{2^8}-Z)=1$. Rabin's criterion proves irreducibility. The sources give the analogous congruence and gcd certificate for $p_1$. For $p_2$, repeated squaring gives $Z^{2^8}\equiv Z^{15}+Z^{10}+Z^3$ and $Z^{2^{16}}\equiv Z$, while the displayed Bézout identity between $p_2$ and $Z^{2^8}-Z$ equals $1$. Rabin's criterion again applies.
lemmas.statement_markdown: The polynomials $p_0(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1$, $p_1(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z+1$, and $p_2(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^9+Z^4+Z^2+1$ are irreducible over $\mathbb F_2$.
lemmas.title: Explicit degree-16 field models

lemmas.proof_markdown: Linearity is immediate. Evaluating at $y=0$ recovers $z_0$, and comparing with the values at the unit vectors recovers $z_1,\ldots,z_{m-1}$, proving injectivity. If the linear part is nonzero, translation by a coordinate on which it is nonzero pairs zeros with ones. The only remaining nonzero case is the constant-one function.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $F/\mathbb F_2$ have basis $1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{m-1}$, and write $z=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}z_i\alpha^i$. The map
$$H(z)_y=z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}z_i y_i,\qquad y\in\mathbb F_2^{m-1},$$
is an $\mathbb F_2$-linear injection with image $\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)$. Its signed sum is $2^{m-1}$ for $z=0$, $-2^{m-1}$ for $z=1$, and $0$ otherwise.
lemmas.title: Affine truth-table spectrum

lemmas.proof_markdown: Both encoders are binary linear and injective, so the concatenation has binary dimension $mK$ and length $N2^{m-1}$. Every nonzero outer word has at least $D_{\rm out}$ nonzero symbols, and each such symbol produces an inner word of weight at least $2^{m-2}$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: If $Q$ is an $[N,K,D_{\rm out}]_{2^m}$ linear code and its symbols are encoded by the affine map $H$ of `affine-truth-table-spectrum`, then the concatenated code is a binary $[N2^{m-1},mK,\ge D_{\rm out}2^{m-2}]_2$ code.
lemmas.title: Affine-inner concatenation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The evaluation map is injective because a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $64$ cannot vanish at all $32768$ points of $A$. Thus the message dimension is $65\cdot16=1040$, while $|A||Y|=2^{30}$. A nonzero polynomial has at most $64$ roots, so at least $32704$ blocks are nonzero; each weighs at least $2^{14}$.

For equality, let $U=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^5\}$ and $L_U(X)=\prod_{u\in U}(X-u)$. The subspace-polynomial computation in `composition-10` gives nine generators for $L_U(A)$, all annihilated by the binary functional with mask `0x007b`, while that functional takes value one on $1$. Hence $1\notin L_U(A)$. The polynomial $L_U$ has exactly the $64$ elements of $U$ as roots and never takes value $1$ elsewhere, so its remaining blocks all have weight $2^{14}$.

A generator matrix is produced by indexing rows by $(j,i)\in\{0,\ldots,64\}\times\{0,\ldots,15\}$ and outputting $C(\alpha^iX^j)$. For each entry, compute $\alpha^ia^j$ modulo $p_0$, extract its coefficient bits, and evaluate the displayed affine form. A bounded number of degree-16 operations per entry gives $O(n)$ time for the fixed $1040$ rows, matching the $1040n$-bit output size.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1)$, let $A=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{14}\}$, and let $H$ be the affine encoder of `affine-truth-table-spectrum`. Then
$$C=\left\{\bigl(H(f(a))\bigr)_{a\in A}:f\in F[X],\ \deg f\le64\right\}$$
is a binary linear $[2^{30},1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2$ code, and its complete generator matrix is output by a deterministic $n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm.
lemmas.title: Canonical dimension-1040 code

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For nonconstant $f$, both $f$ and $f-1$ have at most $64$ roots, so $N_0(f),N_1(f)\le64$. The affine block weights give
$$\operatorname{wt}(C(f))=2^{14}(32768-N_0(f)+N_1(f)).$$
The coefficient constraint defining $B$ excludes the constant polynomial $1$; every other nonzero constant in $B$ is balanced. Finally, $C(1)=\mathbf1$ and every message has a unique decomposition into the hyperplane plus either $0$ or $1$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
In `canonical-rs-affine-code`, let $B$ be the image of messages for which the coefficient of $1$ in the constant coefficient of $f$ is zero. Then $\dim B=1039$, every nonzero $b\in B$ satisfies
$$535{,}822{,}336\le\operatorname{wt}(b)\le537{,}919{,}488,$$
and $C=B\oplus\langle\mathbf1\rangle$.
lemmas.title: Canonical balanced core

lemmas.proof_markdown: Order the $\ell_j$ decreasingly. Projection of $W$ onto the first $K-1$ coordinates has a nonzero kernel vector $w$. Its active blocks have total length at most $M(L-K+1)/L$. For each output bit, its value on $\lambda w_j$, as $\lambda$ ranges over $\mathbb F_Q^*$, is either identically zero or equals one exactly $Q/2$ times. Averaging the weights of the nonzero scalar orbit and using injectivity gives the inequality. At the target parameters, substituting $K=66$ yields a value below $32704\cdot16384$ because $32704\cdot65535-32703\cdot65536=32832>0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $W\le\mathbb F_Q^L$ be $\mathbb F_Q$-linear of dimension $K$, and let $\phi_j:\mathbb F_Q\to\mathbb F_2^{\ell_j}$ be binary-linear maps such that $\Phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_L)$ is injective on $W$. With $M=\sum_j\ell_j$,
$$d(\Phi(W))\le\frac{Q}{2(Q-1)}\frac{L-K+1}{L}M.$$
For $Q=65536$, $L=32768$, and $M\le2^{30}$, every target-meeting such code has $K\le65$ and binary dimension at most $1040$.
lemmas.title: Unequal-block scalar-orbit bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: Exact length gives $N=2^{31-m}$. Distinct-point evaluation requires $N\le2^m$, hence $m\ge16$. Product distance gives $(N-K+1)2^{m-2}\ge(511/1024)N2^{m-1}$, or $K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}$. Direct comparison over $m\ge16$ yields $1040$ at $m=16$, then $561,306,171,100,63,44$ for $m=17,\ldots,22$, and at most $31$ thereafter.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
For an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code over $\mathbb F_{2^m}$ concatenated with $\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)$ at exact length $2^{30}$, every product-distance-certified target code has
$$k\le m\left(1+\left\lfloor2^{22-m}\right\rfloor\right)\le1040.$$
Equality occurs only for $m=16$, outer length $32768$, and outer dimension $65$.
lemmas.title: Exact RS–affine family optimum

lemmas.proof_markdown: The smooth projective normalization of $Y^2+Y=P(X)$ has one rational point above infinity and genus $(d-1)/2$. For each $x$, the equation in $Y$ has two solutions exactly when $\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))=0$. Hence its point count is $q+1+S(P)$. Hasse–Weil gives $|S(P)|\le2g\sqrt q=(d-1)\sqrt q$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $q=2^m$ and let $P\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ have positive odd degree $d$. Then
$$\left|\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_q}(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_2}(P(x))}\right|\le(d-1)\sqrt q.$$
lemmas.title: Odd-polynomial additive Weil bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: Rabin's degree-30 test, using the displayed Frobenius residues at exponents $6,10,15,30$, proves that $T^{30}+T+1$ is irreducible. The parameter space has dimension $1+33\cdot30=991$. A nonzero kernel word would have signed sum $2^{30}$, contradicting the Weil bound $64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21}$. The weight identity gives the claimed distance. The exponent-one layer and the external constant give $\operatorname{RM}(1,30)$; the algebraic degree of the term with exponent $j$ is at most the binary weight of $j$, which is at most six for odd $j\le65$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $K=\mathbb F_2[T]/(T^{30}+T+1)$ and
$$C=\left\{\left(c+\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sum_{j\in\{1,3,\ldots,65\}}a_jx^j\right)\right)_{x\in K}:c\in\mathbb F_2,\ a_j\in K\right\}.$$
Then $C$ is a deterministic binary linear $[2^{30},991,\ge535{,}822{,}336]_2$ code and
$$\operatorname{RM}(1,30)\subset C\subseteq\operatorname{RM}(6,30).$$
lemmas.title: Degree-65 trace-polynomial code

lemmas.proof_markdown: The modulus $T^{15}+T+1$ satisfies Rabin's degree-15 criterion by the displayed degree-$3$ and degree-$5$ coprimality certificates. The signed double sum factors into two endpoint sums. For nonzero $P$, both have odd degree at most $9$, so integrality and the Weil bound give magnitude at most $\lfloor8\sqrt{32768}\rfloor=1448$. Their product is at most $2{,}096{,}704$. Linear-only words are balanced, and the constant-only word is all-one. The correlation bound also excludes a nonlinear kernel, while nondegeneracy of the trace pairing excludes a linear kernel.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(T^{15}+T+1)$ and $P(X)=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9$. The evaluations
$$c_{P,u,v,b}(x,y)=b+\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy),\qquad (x,y)\in F^2,$$
form a deterministic binary linear $[2^{30},91,\ge535{,}822{,}560]_2$ code.
lemmas.title: Complete-bipartite trace-walk code

lemmas.proof_markdown: Constants distinguish the inner functional index, and the polynomials $zX$ then distinguish the evaluation point, so the $2^{30}$ connection functionals are distinct and nonzero. The character indexed by $P$ has eigenvalue $2^{15}(N_0(P)-N_1(P))$. The root bound for $P$ and $P-1$ gives magnitude at most $2^{21}$ except for $P=0,1$, which give $\pm2^{30}$. Injectivity of the code implies that the connection set spans the dual group.
lemmas.statement_markdown: The code in `canonical-rs-affine-code` is the character code of a connected bipartite Cayley graph on $\mathbb F_2^{1040}$ with $2^{30}$ distinct nonzero connection elements. Its spectrum consists of $\pm2^{30}$ and values of magnitude at most $2^{21}$.
lemmas.title: Cayley-character certificate

lemmas.proof_markdown: Interpolate $v$ on $S$ by $p_S$ of degree at most $t-1$, and set $u_\lambda=v+\operatorname{ev}_A(p_S+\lambda h_S)$. Each $u_\lambda$ has the $t$ forced zeros in $S$. At every coordinate outside $S$, its value runs bijectively over $F$ as $\lambda$ varies. Summing the zero and one counts over all $\lambda$ therefore gives equality. Since every pencil member satisfies $N_0-N_1\le t$, equality holds termwise. The multisets of zero-producing and one-producing parameters coincide; equality of their sums yields the reciprocal identity.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $F$ have characteristic two, let $A\subset F$, let $R=\operatorname{ev}_A(F[X]_{\le t})$, and let $v\in F^A\setminus R$. If every $u\in v+R$ satisfies $N_0(u)-N_1(u)\le t$, then for every $t$-element set $S\subset A$,
$$\sum_{a\in A\setminus S}\left(\prod_{s\in S}(a-s)\right)^{-1}=0.$$
lemmas.title: Reciprocal-pencil criterion

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For $R_0=(U\setminus\{0\})\cup\{b\}$, the subspace polynomial is
$$L_U(X)=X^{64}+\mathtt{2e0c}X^{32}+\mathtt{71ee}X^{16}+\mathtt{d9a4}X^8+\mathtt{2198}X^4+\mathtt{c6ca}X^2+\mathtt{6115}X.$$
Its fiber decomposition gives
$$\sum_{a\in A\setminus R_0}G_{R_0}(a)^{-1}=\mathtt{ac5c}+\mathtt{073e}+\mathtt{a2f2}=\mathtt{0990}\ne0.$$
The alternative fixed set in `combinatorial-08` similarly gives `0xe1f0`. Either value contradicts `reciprocal-pencil-criterion` for every coset outside $R$. Any strict additive supercode contains such a coset and hence a word with $N_0-N_1\ge65$, whose binary weight is at most $2^{14}(32768-65)=535{,}805{,}952$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $F=\mathbb F_2[\alpha]/(\alpha^{16}+\alpha^5+\alpha^3+\alpha^2+1)$, $A=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{14}\}$, and $R=\operatorname{ev}_A(F[X]_{\le64})$. Under the fixed coordinatewise affine encoder, every $\mathbb F_2$-linear $D$ satisfying $R\subseteq D\subseteq F^A$ and minimum binary distance at least $535{,}822{,}336$ obeys $D=R$.
lemmas.title: Fixed-inner additive maximality

lemmas.proof_markdown: The equations $\ell(b)=1$ are inconsistent precisely when a binary combination of them has zero left side and right side one, equivalently when an odd subset of $B$ sums to zero. A minimum-cardinality odd zero-sum subset is minimally dependent: deleting a proper even dependence leaves a smaller odd zero-sum subset, and a proper odd dependence contradicts minimality. It would therefore be an odd circuit.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $B\subseteq\mathbb F_2^K\setminus\{0\}$ contain no odd circuit. Then there exists a nonzero linear functional $\ell$ such that $\ell(b)=1$ for every $b\in B$, and the hyperplane $\ker\ell$ is disjoint from $B$.
lemmas.title: Odd-circuit hyperplane expurgation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For $R=D-1$, the one-sided binomial tail $p$ satisfies $2^{2972}p<1083$. Coordinate pairing and the exact tail-to-boundary ratio give every nonprincipal Fourier coefficient of the two-tail indicator magnitude below $q/256$, where $q=2p$. Parity-coset exponential moments bound the expected number of bad odd circuits of sizes $3$ through $255$ by $2^{-27}$; Fourier convolution and Parseval bound the contribution from sizes at least $257$ by $2^{-742}$.

Thus the potential $\Psi(G)=|B(G)|/1084+\sum_sT_s(G)$ has expectation below $1083/1084+2^{-26}<1$. Selecting at each matrix entry a child with no larger exact completion average produces a matrix with $\Psi<1$, so $|B(G)|\le1083$ and there is no bad odd circuit. Apply `odd-circuit-hyperplane` to obtain a $2970$-dimensional subspace avoiding both bad tails; adjoining the all-one word adds one dimension and complements the retained words.
lemmas.statement_markdown: There exists a binary linear $[2^{30},2971,\ge535{,}822{,}336]_2$ code obtained from a $2971\times2^{30}$ matrix whose set of two-tail-bad messages has at most $1083$ elements and contains no odd circuit.
lemmas.title: Conditional-average existence at dimension 2971

lemmas.proof_markdown: For any nonempty finite set $W\subseteq\{0,1\}^M$, apply the same prefix rule to $\Psi(x)=\mathbf1[x\notin W]$. Its initial average is below one, and choosing a child of no larger completion average returns an element of $W$. Thus unrestricted exact completion averages subsume arbitrary exhaustive finite witness search. No structural polynomial-time evaluator is supplied for the dimension-2971 matrix, so the construction does not meet the campaign's $n^{O(1)}$ generator requirement.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Under the requirement that a complete generator matrix be output by a deterministic $n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm and that exhaustive finite witness searches are inadmissible, the unrestricted completion-average selector used in `conditional-average-existence-2971` is not an admissible explicit construction.
lemmas.title: Ineligibility of unrestricted completion averages

lemmas.proof_markdown: Exact lower-tail estimates give $\lambda=2^{2972}q>2090$ and hence $\mathbb E|B|>2089$. For $s=2089$, the exact number of circuits and the Fourier lower bound give $\mathbb ET_{2089}>1$. The size term therefore blocks cutoffs at most $2088$, and the circuit term blocks larger cutoffs. Jensen's inequality gives the same conclusion for the natural exponential tilts. This is only a statement about these potentials.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
At preliminary matrix dimension $2972$, every potential
$$\frac{|B|}{r+1}+\sum_{\substack{s\le r\\s\text{ odd}}}w_sT_s,\qquad w_s\ge1,$$
and every natural exponential tilt specified in `combinatorial-02` has initial expectation at least one.
lemmas.title: Obstruction to the tested dimension-2972 potentials

lemmas.proof_markdown: For each nonzero $u$, expand $S_u^{4096}$. Under $4096$-wise independence, a term has nonzero expectation only when every used index has even multiplicity. Pairing the positions gives $\mathbb ES_u^{4096}\le4095!!\,N^{2048}$. Robbins' bounds give $4095!!<2^{21622}$, so for $K=2954$ the expected union potential is below one. Hence some seed has $|S_u|<2^{21}$ for all nonzero $u$. Adjoining all-one produces the stated dimension. No such seed is explicitly selected by the sources.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Within the specified $4096$-wise-independent polynomial family of $2^{30}$ columns in $\mathbb F_2^{2954}$, there exists a seed for which every nonzero character sum has magnitude below $2^{21}$; the resulting balanced core and all-one augmentation have dimensions $2954$ and $2955$, respectively.
lemmas.title: Limited-independence existence threshold

lemmas.proof_markdown: After omitting any one output, the missing original variable is recovered from the sum output and the remaining originals, so any $t$ outputs are independent uniform. Summing all $t+1$ outputs cancels every original variable twice.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For every factorization $rt=30$, there are $2^{30}$ seeds producing random variables $Y_1,\ldots,Y_{t+1}\in\mathbb F_2^r$ that are $t$-wise independent and satisfy $Y_1+\cdots+Y_{t+1}=0$ identically.
lemmas.title: Wise independence does not control full parity

lemmas.proof_markdown: Character orthogonality leaves only fibers on which $P(x)=0$, giving absolute signed sum at most $64q$ when $P\ne0$. When $P=0$, the word consists of $q$ repetitions of $Q$, so the offset code needs distance at least $16352$. Distinct root-family functions agree in at most $64$ positions, and Singleton gives binary dimension at most $15\cdot65=975$. The degree-three Levenshtein bound gives every binary $[32768,k,\ge16352]$ offset code size at most $2{,}466{,}889<2^{22}$, hence $k\le21$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $q=2^{15}$, let $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathbb F_q^X$ be binary linear with every nonzero member having at most $64$ zeros, and let $W\le\mathbb F_2^X$. If
$$c_{P,Q}(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(yP(x))+Q(x)$$
meets the target for all nonzero $(P,Q)$, then $\dim\mathcal P\le975$, $\dim W\le21$, and the resulting code has dimension at most $996$.
lemmas.title: Independent-offset root-killing ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For the normalized distance distribution $A_i$, character orthogonality gives
$$\sum_iA_iK_j(i)=|C|^{-1}\sum_{|S|=j}\left|\sum_{c\in C}(-1)^{\sum_{r\in S}c_r}\right|^2\ge0.$$
Therefore $\sum_iA_iF(i)\ge f_0|C|$. The minimum-distance assumption makes every nonzero-distance contribution nonpositive, while $A_0=1$, so the same sum is at most $F(0)$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $C$ be a binary code of minimum distance at least $d$. If $F=\sum_jf_jK_j$ has $f_0>0$, $f_j\ge0$ for all $j$, and $F(i)\le0$ for every integer $i\ge d$, then
$$|C|\le\frac{F(0)}{f_0}.$$
lemmas.title: Finite Delsarte polynomial bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: Restrict to the complement of a minimum word $c$. The kernel is exactly $\langle c\rangle$: otherwise two nonzero kernel words differing by $c$ would have weights summing to $\operatorname{wt}(c)$. For a lift with weights $a,b$ on and off the support, the lift and its sum with $c$ give $a+b\ge d$ and $d-a+b\ge d$, so $b\ge\lceil d/2\rceil$. Iteration proves the Griesmer sum.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Every binary linear $[n,k,d]_2$ code has a residual $[n-d,k-1,\ge\lceil d/2\rceil]_2$ code on a minimum word. Consequently
$$n\ge\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil\frac d{2^i}\right\rceil.$$
lemmas.title: Binary residual and Griesmer bounds

lemmas.proof_markdown: For $(8192,4090)$, the cubic $(y-12)(y+630)(y+632)$ has Krawtchouk coefficients $(5462080,407590,2500,6)$ and yields $116581$. At length $8193$, the cubics $(y-13)(y+585)(y+587)$ and $(y-17)(y+455)(y+457)$ yield $125297$ and $161040$. For length $32768$, parity extension and the cubic $(t-5)(t+5459)(t+5463)$ bound cardinality below $2^{18}$ at distance $16381$. Independently, two residualizations of a hypothetical linear $[32768,18,16381]_2$ code yield a zero-padded $[8196,16,4096]_2$ code, while $(y-4)(y+1640)^2$ bounds its size below $49253$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
The following bounds hold:
$$A_2(8192,4090)\le116581,$$
$$A_2(8193,4090)\le125297,$$
$$A_2(8193,4088)\le161040.$$
Moreover, no binary code of length $32768$, cardinality $2^{18}$, and distance at least $16381$ exists.
lemmas.title: Finite inner-code exclusions

lemmas.proof_markdown: For distance $8190$, parity extension first bounds the possible actual minimum. Residualization gives either a $[4098,14,2048]_2$ branch, excluded by the displayed gap cubic, or a forced chain ending in a forbidden $[67,8,32]_2$ code; the published exact value is $N_2(8,32)=68$. For distance $8189$, the analogous branches either reach the same cubic obstruction or a forbidden $[132,9,64]_2$ code; the published exact value is $N_2(9,64)=133$. Larger distances are already covered by these arguments and monotonicity.
lemmas.statement_markdown: No binary linear $[16384,16,d]_2$ code exists for $d\ge8189$.
lemmas.title: Rank-16 length-16384 endpoint exclusion

lemmas.proof_markdown: Griesmer and field-size constraints reduce every case above $1040$ to inner length $8192$, $16384$, or $32768$. The degree-three spherical/Delsarte bounds eliminate length $8192$, length $32768$, and ranks at least $19$ at length $16384$. The residual value $N_2(9,64)=133$ gives the rank-16 distance ceiling $8188$; parity extension gives ceilings $8188$ and $8184$ for ranks $17$ and $18$. Exact rounding then gives outer dimension at most $97,97,65$, respectively, so the products are $1552,1649,1170$. If the inner code contains all-one, quotienting by complements and applying the Gram-rank bound forces its relevant rank to be at most $15$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let a binary linear $[2^s,m,d]_2$ inner code be concatenated with an ordinary Reed–Solomon $[L,K,L-K+1]_{2^m}$ code, where $1\le m\le30$ and $L\le\min(2^m,2^{30-s})$, and zero-pad to length $2^{30}$. If $d(L-K+1)\ge535{,}822{,}336$, then $mK\le1649$. If the inner code contains the all-one word, then $mK\le1040$.
lemmas.title: Ordinary RS product ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown: Given the inner encoder, identify its $17$-dimensional message space with $\mathbb F_{2^{17}}$ and concatenate it with the explicit Reed–Solomon code $[65536,97,65440]_{2^{17}}$. Length and dimension multiply, and the product distance is $8188\cdot65440=535{,}822{,}720$. The required inner code is not constructed in the sources.
lemmas.statement_markdown: If a deterministic polynomial-time generable binary linear $[16384,17,8188]_2$ code exists, then a deterministic binary linear $[2^{30},1649,\ge535{,}822{,}720]_2$ code exists.
lemmas.title: Conditional dimension-1649 gateway

lemmas.proof_markdown: The chosen complements give a unique decomposition in each block, so the encoder is linear and injective. In a nonzero codeword, let $i$ be the first active level. Every later contribution to block $j$ lies in $B_{i+1}$, and the block weight is therefore at least the coset weight $\omega_i(e_j)$. Summing over blocks proves the weighted bound; replacing every nonzero coset weight by $\lambda_i$ gives the product form.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $B_0\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq B_s=0$ be a binary linear flag with complement sections $\sigma_i$, and let $E_i$ be binary-linear outer constituents of dimensions $\kappa_i$. With
$$\omega_i(u)=\min_{v\in B_{i+1}}\operatorname{wt}(\sigma_i(u)+v),$$
the generalized concatenation has dimension $\sum_i\kappa_i$ and
$$d(C)\ge\min_i\min_{e\in E_i\setminus\{0\}}\sum_j\omega_i(e_j)\ge\min_i\Delta_i\lambda_i.$$
lemmas.title: Weighted-shell concatenation

lemmas.proof_markdown: Every nonconstant affine word has weight $16384$, and the only heavier nonzero word is all-one. Thus every ordinary shell requires outer distance at least $32704$ and contributes at most $65m_i$ dimensions by puncturing/Singleton. Summing the $16$ quotient dimensions gives $1040$. If the repetition shell is isolated, the other levels contribute at most $975$; the cubic Delsarte bound at parameters $[32768,c,\ge16352]_2$ gives $c\le21$ for the repetition constituent, totaling $996$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Every generalized concatenation through a full $\operatorname{RM}(1,15)$ flag certified by the first-active-level product bound has dimension at most $1040$. If the repetition line is isolated as a separate level, its dimension is at most $996$.
lemmas.title: Reed–Muller flag ceilings

lemmas.proof_markdown: Shorten on any $65$ blocks. Their combined rank is at most $1040$, so the shortened code retains dimension at least $k-1040$. Removing the zero blocks leaves length $32703\cdot32768=1{,}071{,}611{,}904$ and unchanged distance. Since twice the distance exceeds this length, Plotkin bounds its cardinality by $32704<2^{15}$, hence its binary dimension by $14$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $C\le\mathbb F_2^{2^{30}}$ be partitioned into $32768$ blocks of length $32768$, and suppose every block projection of $C$ has rank at most $16$. If $d(C)\ge535{,}822{,}336$, then $\dim C\le1054$.
lemmas.title: Arbitrarily coupled rank-16 block ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown: For a direct sum, every positive-rank block must have length at least $D$. If one of two blocks has rank at least two, the identity $\operatorname{wt}(x)+\operatorname{wt}(y)+\operatorname{wt}(x+y)\le2n_i$ forces its length to be at least $3D/2$, incompatible with a second block of length at least $D$. For a nontrivial binary factor, average weight gives relative distance at most $2/3$; tensor distances multiply. For the Plotkin transform, $d=\min(2d(U),d(V))$, so $V$ would need relative distance $511/512>2/3$ and thus rank at most one.
lemmas.statement_markdown: At length $2^{30}$ and distance at least $535{,}822{,}336$: (i) every coordinate-interleaved direct sum with at least two positive-rank constituents has total dimension at most $2$; (ii) a tensor product of two binary linear factors of dimension at least two cannot meet the target; and (iii) a one-step Plotkin transform can gain at most one dimension from its second constituent.
lemmas.title: Elementary composition obstructions

lemmas.proof_markdown: Translate the seeds by $d_1$ and write $W_a=\sum_i(-1)^{a(d_i+d_1)}$. The output sum factors as $W_a^2$, so the target implies $|W_a|\le1448$. Fourier orthogonality expresses the $174$th moment as the number of zero-XOR ordered $174$-tuples. Counting tuples obtained from $87$ distinct indices, each repeated twice, gives $L=\binom{32768}{87}174!/2^{87}$. Exact integer estimates yield $L-1448^{174}>2^{1825}$ and numerator $32768^{174}=2^{2610}$, hence $2^k<2^{785}$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For any ordered multiset of $32768$ elements of a binary vector space, if the character code of all ordered XOR pairs meets the target, then its homogeneous dimension is at most $784$. Adjoining the all-one word gives dimension at most $785$.
lemmas.title: Complete XOR-square ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown: Padding preserves distance. Puncturing $L-n$ fixed coordinates loses at most $L-n$ distance; if the resulting lower bound is positive, a kernel word would have raw weight below the certified raw distance, so dimension is preserved. Substitution and rearrangement give the displayed absolute-value form. Whole-symbol shortening and puncturing of an MDS outer code merely replace its parameters by another MDS pair already covered by varying $(N,K)$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let a binary $[L,k,\delta]_2$ code be adjusted to length $n$ by zero padding when $L\le n$ or fixed puncturing when $L\ge n$. The generic certificate gives distance at least $D$ exactly when
$$L-2\delta+|n-L|\le n-2D.$$
If $D>0$, the puncturing branch preserves dimension.
lemmas.title: Blind length-adjustment identity

lemmas.proof_markdown: Combining Griesmer with the padding and puncturing inequalities reduces $2\le m\le30$ to an exact finite loop. It leaves $57$ inner pairs: $7,35,13,1,1$ for $m=17,18,19,20,21$. Forty-nine attain the Griesmer sum and are excluded by Logacev's strict improvement in the applicable range. The seven rank-17 pairs puncture to the cubic-impossible length-$8192$ case. Residual weight classification, projective Pless moments, and at-most-one-heavy-word arguments exclude the remaining rank-18 and rank-19 defect-one cases.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For $2\le m\le30$, no equal-inner concatenation of a binary $[\ell,m,d]_2$ code with an ordinary or once-extended Reed–Solomon outer code can be certified to have dimension at least $2972$ and distance at least $535{,}822{,}336$ using product distance followed by zero padding or generic fixed-puncture loss.
lemmas.title: Equal-inner RS obstruction at dimension 2972

lemmas.proof_markdown: A seed with $A_sx=0$ gives an all-zero block; every other seed gives a balanced nonzero linear functional. This proves the exact weight and bias formulas. For a source uniform on $\{0,x\}$, every killed seed creates an atom of mass $1/D$ whereas a distribution of min-entropy $d+1$ has atoms of mass at most $1/(2D)$. Thus total variation is at least $z(x)/(2D)$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $A_s:\mathbb F_2^K\to\mathbb F_2^m$, $s\in[D]$, be binary-linear, and define $c_x(s,u)=\langle u,A_sx\rangle$. If $z(x)=|\{s:A_sx=0\}|$, then
$$\operatorname{wt}(c_x)=2^{m-1}(D-z(x)),\qquad \frac1{D2^m}\sum_{s,u}(-1)^{c_x(s,u)}=\frac{z(x)}D.$$
A strong entropy-one lossless condenser of error $\eta$ satisfies $z(x)/D\le2\eta$ for every nonzero $x$.
lemmas.title: Condenser-to-character conversion

lemmas.proof_markdown: The strict Plotkin argument for a $2$-universal family gives at most $qD$ messages, yielding dimensions $30$ and $31$ in the homogeneous and affine conversions. For AGHP powering, bias equals the evaluation-root fraction; exact length reduces the optimization to $(30-a)(2^{a-9}+1)$, maximized at $975$. Univariate affine hashing is exactly the RS–affine optimization and reaches $1040$. Substitution in the GUV seed formula and AM–GM gives seed length at least $33$ before output enumeration.
lemmas.statement_markdown: At exact length $2^{30}$, the audited standard conversions satisfy: ordinary $2$-universal hashing has dimension at most $31$; direct AGHP polynomial powering has dimension at most $975$; univariate affine polynomial hashing has dimension at most $1040$; and the direct GUV entropy-one specialization requires at least $33$ seed bits.
lemmas.title: Standard extractor-family ceilings

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Every parity-walk label lies in the span of the outer labels, so rank cannot increase. For an undirected $D$-regular rotation multigraph, integral port multiplicities give $\operatorname{tr}(P^2)\ge m/D$, whereas the spectral bound gives $\operatorname{tr}(P^2)\le1+(m-1)\lambda^2$.

Using this inequality, the Ta-Shma compatibility conditions have no contracting case: small widths make the block factor at least one, widths $4$ through $9$ force it above three, and larger widths contradict compatibility. For Cohen–Cohen, contraction forces outer spectral value below $1/40$, hence degree at least $631$ and width at least three, producing at least $1041\cdot631^3$ rows. For the free-expander schedule, $\kappa=1$ does not contract, while $\kappa\ge2$ forces lift factor at least $2^{32}$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: No complete-output specialization certified by the audited Ta-Shma wide-replacement theorem, Cohen–Cohen Gray-register theorem, or Hsieh–Mohanty–Zhang free-expander schedule has rank at least $1041$, absolute bias at most $1/512$, and at most $2^{30}$ output coordinates.
lemmas.title: Complete-walk finite no-fit theorem

lemmas.proof_markdown: The distance certificate requires $L-a\ge535{,}822{,}336/64=8{,}372{,}224$, and Riemann–Roch eligibility gives $a\ge g$, so $L\ge8{,}372{,}224+g$. Hasse–Weil and the required $L+1$ rational points give $L\le256+32g$. Hence $g\ge270{,}064$ and $L\ge8{,}642{,}288$. The exact length condition instead gives $L\le\lfloor(2^{30}-16512)/128\rfloor=8{,}388{,}479$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: No specialization satisfying the hypotheses of the fixed $\mathbb F_{256}$ quotient-coupled Construction 4.1 can satisfy both $128L+16{,}512\le2^{30}$ and its certified-distance inequality $64(L-a)\ge535{,}822{,}336$.
lemmas.title: Fixed quotient-coupled AG-port obstruction

lemmas.proof_markdown: In characteristic two, $X^{2^{30}}-1=(X+1)^{2^{30}}$. A dimension-$k$ cyclic ideal is generated by $(X+1)^{2^{30}-k}$. If $k\ge4$, it contains $(X+1)^{2^{30}-4}$. Lucas' theorem gives this word weight $2^{\operatorname{wt}_2(2^{30}-4)}=2^{28}$, below the target.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Every binary cyclic code of length $2^{30}$ and minimum distance at least $535{,}822{,}336$ has dimension at most $3$.
lemmas.title: Exact-length cyclic-code ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown: For a relative difference set, coset injectivity gives $a\ge30$. Counting ordered differences gives $2^{30}(2^{30}-1)=\lambda2^s(2^a-1)$. Comparing $2$-adic valuations gives $s\le30$, while Mersenne divisibility gives $a\mid30$; hence $a=30$ and $a+s\le60$. For a simple partial difference set, the strongly regular identity bounds the ambient order by $2^{60}+1$ when $\mu>0$; $\mu=0$ would require a Cayley component of order $2^{30}+1$, impossible in an elementary abelian $2$-group.
lemmas.statement_markdown: A relative difference set of size $2^{30}$ in an elementary abelian $2$-group has ambient binary dimension at most $60$. A simple unweighted partial-difference-set Cayley character construction with $2^{30}$ connection elements also has ambient dimension at most $60$.
lemmas.title: Difference-set ambient-dimension ceilings

lemmas.proof_markdown: For $h$ simplex copies with proper subspaces deleted, the parameters satisfy $n=h(2^m-1)-\sum_i(2^{u_i}-1)$ and $d_0=h2^{m-1}-\sum_i2^{u_i-1}$. Codimension-intersection bounds eliminate all but four exceptional $(m,h)$ pairs. Exact power-of-two accounting eliminates $(16,7)$, $(17,8)$, $(17,16)$, and $(18,8)$ as detailed in the source.
lemmas.statement_markdown: The standard whole-subspace $h$-copy Solomon–Stiffler deletion certificate produces none of the inner parameters $[16384,16,\ge8185]_2$, $[16384,17,\ge8184]_2$, or $[16384,18,\ge8184]_2$.
lemmas.title: Solomon–Stiffler gateway obstruction

lemmas.proof_markdown: For reduced principal parts, a pole of odd order $d_P$ contributes at most $(d_P+1)/2$ residue-field coefficients. Thus the binary phase-space dimension is at most $1+15R$. Riemann–Hurwitz gives $2g\le R-2$, and Hasse–Weil gives signed correlation at most $(R-2)2^{15}$. The target correlation cap $2^{21}$ forces $R\le66$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For the fixed-pole reduced Artin–Schreier trace families described in `composition-07`, if distance is certified only through the generic conductor/genus Hasse–Weil bound, then the target forces conductor quantity $R\le66$ and binary dimension at most $1+15R\le991$.
lemmas.title: Fixed-conductor Artin–Schreier ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The distribution
$$A_0=1,\quad A_{16381}=26180051/100,\quad A_{18725}=34249/100$$
is nonnegative and totals $2^{18}$. The recurrence $P_{j+1}=tP_j-j(32768-j+1)P_{j-1}$ gives strictly positive Krawtchouk transforms for $j=1,\ldots,5$, with the exact values listed in `combinatorial-10`. Weak duality therefore prevents a degree-at-most-five dual certificate from giving a smaller cardinality bound.
lemmas.statement_markdown: No Delsarte certificate using only Krawtchouk degrees at most five can prove $A_2(32768,16381)<2^{18}$.
lemmas.title: Degree-five direct-LP insufficiency

lemmas.proof_markdown: Distinct outer evaluation points force $m\ge17$. Product distance forces $d\ge\lceil535{,}822{,}336/131072\rceil=4088$. Parity extension together with the two length-$8193$ cubic bounds forces $m\le17$ and excludes $d\ge4089$ at dimension $17$. Thus $m=17$ and $d=4088$. Since the target equals $4088\cdot131072$, the outer distance must be $131072$, so $K=1$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let a binary linear $[8192,m,d]_2$ code be concatenated with a generalized Reed–Solomon $[131072,K,131073-K]_{2^m}$ code. If $d(131073-K)\ge535{,}822{,}336$, then $m=17$, $d=4088$, $K=1$, and the concatenated dimension is $17$.
lemmas.title: The 8192-by-131072 RS product cap

lemmas.proof_markdown: The exact classical specializations give dimensions $975$ for AGHP powering, $991$ for the augmented trace/BCH construction, and smaller values for the audited Hermitian and norm–trace constructions. The standard RS–affine family is maximized at $1040$. The complete-output wide-replacement and free-expander theorems fail their finite length or contraction requirements. The remaining recent trace-AG and concatenation results either retain unavailable constants or use random constituents. This conclusion is restricted to the constructions and certificates enumerated in the two source audits.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Among the classical and 2017–2026 balanced-code constructions and finite certificate specializations enumerated in `composition-09` and `literature-sota-0001`, no campaign-admissible code at the immutable target has dimension exceeding $1040$.
lemmas.title: Scoped balanced-code SOTA audit
